title: ARC Control Control Definition
description: A governance control: the assurance it provides, how it is checked, what a pass does not tell you, and whether ARC can decide it at all. `assurance` is the field that keeps the model honest — only an `automated` control can be decided from ARC's own records; a `deployment` or `manual` control needs a dated human attestation and reports `not_assessable` without one, never a pass.

id.description: Operator-facing control id, cited in reports and framework mappings.

version.description: Bumped when the procedure or scope changes. A result is only interpretable against the procedure that produced it.

objective.description: The assurance the control provides, in one sentence an auditor can read.

procedure.description: Exactly what is checked. For an automated control this describes the implemented assertion; otherwise it is the instruction to the human or deployment reviewer.

assurance.description: `automated`: ARC decides it deterministically from its own records. `deployment`: the answer depends on facts outside ARC's records, such as network routes or credential scope. `manual`: a human judgement.

limitations.description: What a pass does not tell you. Required and non-empty: these travel with every result and every export, so the caveat arrives attached to the green tick rather than in a document beside it.
